examples.name: Example 1 circular arch
examples.about: A laboratory arch traced over its photograph with the three-point tool, in kg-cm, carrying one applied load.

examples.name: Example 1 circular arch minimum thrust
examples.about: The same arch at its least thrust: the line rides the extrados at the haunches and the intrados at the crown.

examples.name: Example 1 circular arch maximum thrust
examples.about: And at its greatest, where the pattern inverts. The two together are the admissible band, drawn.

examples.name: Example 2 Heyman arch
examples.about: Seven voussoirs drawn corner by corner over a figure, with both ends of the line imposed at the springings.

examples.name: Example 3 Delicate arch sunset
examples.about: Delicate Arch, Utah: eight blocks drawn over a photograph. A natural arch stands by the same theorem a built one does.

examples.name: Example 4 Landscape Arch Utah
examples.about: Landscape Arch, the longest natural span in the world, traced intrados and extrados into fifty voussoirs. Carries its own notes.

examples.name: Example 6 Arc boutant Notre Dame de Paris
examples.about: A flying buttress cut from a traced outline, with blocks added by hand. Not one chain, and the panel says which pair does not touch.

examples.name: Example 5 flying arch
examples.about: A flyer with its pier and pinnacle: three free ends, so no ordering of it is a chain. What branches off loads the arch rather than belonging to it.

examples.name: Example 7 San Pietro Giovanni Poleni
examples.about: Poleni's dome of St Peter's, cut as a lune rather than a barrel: the weights follow the width, and the two idealisations of one drawing part company. Five groups, two applied loads, and not one chain.
